title: Ecofriendly Fire Retardant and Rot Resistance Finishing of Jute Fabric Using Tin and Boron Based Compound
journal: Journal of The Institution of Engineers (India): Series E 98(1), 25–31
source_version: Author-posted publisher e-offprint, publicly indexed original full text
composition: Conventionally hydrogen-peroxide-bleached plain-weave jute; 63 ends/dm, 59 picks/dm; warp 195 tex, weft 214 tex; 0.80 mm thickness
TGA_specimen_preparation: Finely crushed jute fibers taken from the corresponding control and treated jute fabrics, as explicitly stated in the own TGA methods. Pan, gas flow, and additional conditioning are not reported.
source_material_form_TGA_raw: Control and treated jute fibre samples, finely crushed, taken out from corresponding control and treated jute fabrics
LOI_method: ASTM D2863-77; standard LOI tester manufactured by S C Dey & Co., Kolkata
LOI_specimen_preparation: Selected untreated and treated fabrics. LOI specimen dimensions and repeat count are unreported; 15 cm × 5 cm dimensions belong to the 45-degree inclined burning test.
source_numeric_evidence_description: Own TG discussion on printed p 30 explicitly gives residue at 500 °C as 27% for the 20% stannate/20% boric-acid jute treatment. Table 4 mass loss 73% corroborates, but the canonical residue is taken directly from prose. Own initial LOI 34 is tabulated in Tables 2–3. Control numerical TG is held for a figure/table conflict.
TG_locator: TGA Study of FR Treated and Untreated Jute Fabric, printed p 30: explicit R500 6 and 27; Table 4 and Figure 1, printed p 29
LOI_locator: Table 1 control, printed p 28; Table 2 initial double-bath 20/20 treatment, p 28; Table 3 initial and washed rows, p 29
conditions_locator: Materials and Methods, printed pp 26–27: fabric, two-stage pad-dry finishing, own LOI and TGA methods
source_location: Public author-uploaded original publisher e-offprint, printed pp 25–31, complete indexed original text and all Tables 1–4 reviewed. Original PDF bytes and table page pixels unavailable; no PDF hash or table pixel claim.
pairing_evidence: The TG prose explicitly identifies the double-bath 20% sodium stannate plus 20% boric acid fabric, with direct R500 27%. Tables 1–3 give own measured initial LOIs for this same recipe; Table 3 separately labels washed states. TGA methods explicitly bridge finely crushed fiber aliquots to their source fabric.
limitations: One bounded initial double-bath fabric state only, pending independent original-source QA. Source reports reagent application percentages as on weight of fabric; these are not measured retained add-on. Initial drying duration, boric-acid bath temperature, gas flow, pan, conditioning and TG/LOI repeats are unreported. Separate stannate-only and boric-acid-only TG rows do not identify their treatment concentration and remain held. Double-bath 15/15 has LOI 29 in prose versus 27 in Table 2; 25/25 has 34.5 in prose versus 34 in Table 2, and these states have no matching exact TG. Washed samples in Table 3 are excluded because TGA is not reported for them. The treated R500 value 27 is explicit original prose, not a graph estimate or computed complement. The control R500 value 6 is source-reported but held because Figure 1 curve a/c endpoints contradict the equal Table 4 residual values. No graph-derived substitute is used. Table 2 labels boric acid as % owf while prose also says % solution; both are retained without conversion to retained add-on. Other Table 4 mass-loss percentages remain raw. No TG Tmax is supplied. Prior 2011 jute studies are cited and need sample-scoped reuse comparison if later proposed; no values or preparation imported from them. Public e-offprint bytes returned 403, so only separately hashed original indexed evidence is available.
source_sample_label: Stannate and boric acid treated jute fabric
sample_state: Jute with sodium stannate 20% owf then boric acid 20% owf, initial
washing_state: Initial after double-bath pad-dry-pad-dry preparation; no durability wash
treatment_chemistry: Sodium stannate trihydrate (Na2SnO3·3H2O) followed by boric acid (H3BO3)
treatment_method: Pad the bleached fabric with aqueous sodium stannate using two dips and two nips to 100% weight pickup, then dry at 100 °C. Pad the dried fabric with hot aqueous boric acid using two dips and two nips to 100% weight pickup, then dry at 100 °C. Use 20% owf sodium stannate and 20% owf boric acid as source-labelled application levels; retained add-on is not reported. Drying duration and hot boric-acid bath temperature are not given; no extra curing or preparation rinse is stated. Table 2 labels boric acid application as % owf, while the prose also calls the boric acid level % solution; both source descriptions are preserved, and neither is converted into bath mass fraction or retained add-on.
